excerpt: El Salto Waterfall in El Naranjo, SLP, has turquoise pools you can swim in year-round. Prices, hours, how to get there from Ciudad Valles and how to pair it with El Aguacate in one day.
contentHtml:
El Salto Waterfall (Cascada El Salto) is a waterfall more than 40 meters high in the municipality of El Naranjo, in the northern part of the Huasteca Potosina. El Salto stands out for the contrast between its limestone walls and the deep turquoise of the water that fills its natural pools, something many travelers don't know about when they plan their trip through the state of San Luis Potosí. El Naranjo is one of the least-traveled municipalities along the Huasteca corridor, which keeps this waterfall a genuinely authentic stop in a region that draws more visitors every season. The most common question: is it worth combining El Salto in El Naranjo with El Aguacate Waterfall in one day, or is it better to visit them separately?

This guide answers exactly that. You'll find updated prices for 2026, a breakdown of entry costs — individual admission from $50 MXN — how to combine both waterfalls, and what sets the El Naranjo waterfalls apart from the other water destinations in the Huasteca Potosina. In high season (September–October), arriving early and planning each stop carefully is essential.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: October 2026. If you'd rather have everything sorted before you leave home, check out our all-inclusive packages to visit El Salto Waterfall.

El Salto and El Aguacate waterfalls: what to see in El Naranjo, SLP

What is El Salto Waterfall, and why does it stand out among the El Naranjo waterfalls?

El Salto Waterfall is part of a river system that runs down through the mountains in the municipality of El Naranjo, San Luis Potosí. Its main drop feeds a turquoise pool where you can swim year-round. The depth in the middle is around 4 meters, enough for jumping in from the rocks along the sides. Admission in 2026 is $50 MXN per person, with an extra $120 MXN for the shared boat ride through the canyon.

The groups we take to El Salto in El Naranjo usually arrive before 9:00 a.m. to find the pools less crowded and the morning light reflecting off the rock. If you want to combine your visit with an organized trip down the turquoise canyon, the closest option in both experience and location is to book the Cascadas del Meco tour, which includes both Meco Waterfall (Cascada del Meco) and a stop at El Salto, from $1,700 MXN per person.

El Aguacate Waterfall: the stop that rounds out the day

El Aguacate Waterfall (Cascada El Aguacate) is in the municipality of Tamasopo, about 3 km north of town and 75 minutes from Ciudad Valles on the highway to San Luis Potosí. Its name comes from the wild avocado trees that grow in the ravine. The falls are narrower than El Salto, but the surrounding vegetation makes it a visually different setting, and cooler in the afternoon. Access to the El Aguacate area costs $50 MXN per person, and the site is open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. every day of the week during high season.

Combining El Aguacate with El Salto in one day makes for a long day, because they're in different municipalities: leave Ciudad Valles before 8:00 a.m. and reach El Aguacate before it closes at 5:00 p.m. For more on seasons and weather in the region, read our guide to the Huasteca Potosina in October: weather, rivers and what to expect.

El Salto Waterfall in 2026: prices, hours and the experience

The experience on site: what to expect when you arrive

First-time visitors to El Salto usually stay longer than they planned. The main pool sits at about 22–24 °C all year, so it's comfortable even in the coolest months. According to local guides, the waterfall reaches its highest flow in September and October, when the water comes down hard enough to form a curtain you can hear from the parking lot. In the dry season (March–May), the waterfall shrinks considerably, but the pools keep their color and depth.

The facilities are basic: a guarded parking area, simple restrooms and a couple of family-run eateries (comedores) serving beef soup (caldo de res) and fresh fruit water (agua de frutas). There are no ATMs on site; everything is paid in cash. If you're not sure what else to bring, see available tours in the Huasteca Potosina to confirm what's included and the logistics before you go.

How much does it cost to visit El Salto Waterfall in 2026?

Here is the full cost breakdown for 2026: site admission $50 MXN per person; camping $150 MXN per tent per night; shared boat ride through the canyon $120 MXN. Our Cascadas del Meco tour, which combines Meco Waterfall and El Salto, costs $1,700 MXN per person; kids 4–7 pay 50 %, ages 3 and under ride free (they still take a seat) and 8 and up pay the adult price. Cash only at the ticket booth and for every service on the property.

If you're traveling as a family and want to compare total budget options for the Huasteca Potosina, our guide to how much the Huasteca Potosina costs has the full breakdown by type of traveler. If you prefer everything arranged from home, our packages with lodging and transportation include entry to El Salto with no extra charges on site.

Tips before visiting El Salto in El Naranjo and El Aguacate Waterfall

Visiting El Salto in El Naranjo takes different logistics than other places in the Huasteca Potosina: access is more remote, services on site are limited, and cell signal is spotty for the last few kilometers. These tips come from the experiences of real travelers we look after every season.

  • Bring enough cash: the site doesn't take cards or bank transfers. Budget at least $500 MXN per person for admission, the boat ride, food and an extra drink or two.
  • Leave Ciudad Valles early: the drive takes 110 minutes. Leaving at 6:00 a.m. gets you there for the 8:00 a.m. opening, so you can enjoy the pools before the biggest crowds. Check the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina for your dates.
  • The right clothes and footwear: water sandals or neoprene water shoes; the bottom of the pools has sharp rocks. Pack a change of clothes in a waterproof bag, because the shared boat splashes. Go through the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle before you pack.
  • Biodegradable sunscreen: regular sunscreen isn't allowed in the pools, to protect water quality. Bring only oxybenzone-free mineral formulas.
  • Best season for El Aguacate Waterfall: go between September and November, when both waterfalls are at their fullest and the ravine is at its greenest. From December to February the water drops and some trails get slippery with the morning dew.

How do you get to El Salto Waterfall from Ciudad Valles?

The route from Ciudad Valles to El Salto in El Naranjo is one of the most direct in the northern Huasteca Potosina, though the last stretches need your attention. The groups we organize in high season travel in convoy from Ciudad Valles to better handle cattle crossings and the loose-gravel stretches off the main highway. Knowing the road ahead of time saves you delays and keeps you from arriving outside opening hours.

Recommended route from Ciudad Valles, step by step

From Ciudad Valles, take the federal highway toward El Naranjo (~90 km, about 90 minutes under normal conditions). When you reach El Naranjo, follow the signs toward Ciudad del Maíz; the last 8 km to the El Salto entrance are paved and in good shape in 2026. All in all, the drive from Ciudad Valles takes 110 minutes. There's no direct public transportation to the waterfall. Without your own vehicle, the cheapest option is the Cascadas del Meco tour, which includes round-trip transportation and the stop at El Salto for $1,700 MXN per person.

Transportation and access options: 2026 comparison

For travelers without a vehicle, the only practical option is an organized tour with transportation included, since El Naranjo's shared taxis don't always go all the way to the site entrance. If you have a car, check your tire pressure before you leave: while the final paved stretch is in good shape, the optional dirt road to El Aguacate Waterfall can get muddy in the rainy season. Frequently asked questions about El Salto Waterfall

What's the difference between El Salto Waterfall and El Aguacate Waterfall?

El Salto is the main waterfall in El Naranjo's river system, with deep turquoise pools you can swim in year-round. El Aguacate is a narrower waterfall set in a small canyon in Tamasopo, 75 minutes from Ciudad Valles, surrounded by dense tropical vegetation. They complement each other, although visiting both in the same day makes for a long day because they're in different municipalities.

How much does it cost to get into El Salto Waterfall in 2026?

General admission is $50 MXN per person in 2026. The shared boat ride through the turquoise canyon adds another $120 MXN. If you want to camp, the camping fee is $150 MXN per tent per night. Everything is paid in cash; there's no card terminal on site.

What's the best season to visit El Salto in El Naranjo?

The ideal season is September–October, when the waterfall has its highest flow thanks to the summer rains. The turquoise pools are open year-round, but in the dry season (March–May) the waterfall loses much of its force. To plan around weather and events, see our guide to the Huasteca Potosina in October.

Is it safe to visit the El Naranjo waterfalls with kids or as a couple?

Yes, with the right precautions. The pools at El Salto have shallow areas suitable for young children, and the site is supervised during opening hours (8:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m.). Life jackets are recommended for kids under 10; some local vendors rent them on site. For couples, the boat ride through the turquoise canyon is the activity first-time visitors recommend most.

Can you camp at El Salto Waterfall?

Yes. The site has a designated camping area on the property, with access to basic restrooms and night security in high season. It costs $150 MXN per tent per night. It's the ideal option if you want to get up early and reach the pools before other visitors, or catch the sunrise over the canyon. Bring all the food you'll need, since the on-site eateries close around 5:00 p.m. and there are no stores nearby.

If your itinerary includes several days in the area, pairing El Salto with the Minas Viejas Waterfalls (Cascadas de Minas Viejas) or the Micos Waterfalls (Cascadas de Micos) makes a complete water route without repeating scenery. For a more technical experience, 45 minutes from Ciudad Valles, Rafting on the Tampaón River, at $1,950 MXN per person, is the natural complement to a day of canyons and turquoise water in the Huasteca Potosina.
